svg.title: The five pitfalls that erode projected RFID labor savings, each with its counter
svg.desc: Five recurring pitfalls behind teams reporting only 60% of projected RFID labor savings, paired with counters: freed labor re-deployed only halfway, since typical re-absorption is 50-70% — plan the destination workflow before go-live; tag-environment mismatch on metal- or liquid-rich SKUs dropping dock-door read rates from 99% to 85% — validate every tag-product combination against the Auburn ARC-tested inlay list; antenna alignment drift from forklift impacts, the documented 3PL's months 8-9 accuracy dip — run a monthly antenna-position audit, that fix took 90 minutes; missing middleware deduplication sending hundreds of duplicate reads per pallet to the WMS until operators revert to manual scans — filter EPC streams with Impinj ItemSense or Zebra Savanna; and skipped change management, the single most-cited cause of ROI shortfall — run a 30-60-day pilot in one zone with before/after time studies.
svg.text: 'WE GOT 60% OF THE PROJECTED SAVINGS' — A POST-MORTEM
Five ways the projection erodes — and the counter for each
WHAT ERODES THE NUMBER
THE COUNTER
Freed labor re-deployed only halfway
typical re-absorption is 50-70%, not 100%
Plan the destination workflow — QA, returns,
problem-solving — before go-live
Tag-environment mismatch
metal- or liquid-rich SKUs: dock-door read rates fall from 99% to 85%
Validate every tag-product combination against
the Auburn ARC-tested inlay list first
Antenna alignment drift
forklift impacts: the documented 3PL dipped below 99% in months 8-9
Monthly antenna-position audit in the
maintenance calendar — that fix took 90 minutes
No middleware deduplication
hundreds of duplicate reads per pallet; operators stop trusting the data
Filter EPC streams (Impinj ItemSense, Zebra
Savanna) before the WMS ever sees them
Change management skipped
the single most-cited cause of ROI shortfall
Run a 30-60-day pilot in one zone with before/after
time studies; let the operators present the results
None of the five is the physics failing — the tags read fine; the plan met the org chart.
